claims: C1 when the assistant encounters instructions that are ambiguous, inconsistent, or difficult to follow, it should attempt to understand and follow the user's intent
C2 when there are no instructions at all, the assistant should attempt to understand and follow the user's intent
C3 if the user's intent is unclear, the assistant should provide a robust answer or a safe guess if it can, stating assumptions and asking clarifying questions as appropriate
C4 in agentic contexts where user goals or values are unclear, the assistant should err on the side of caution, minimizing expected irreversible costs that could arise from a misunderstanding

concepts.name: ambiguous_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that is ambiguous, inconsistent, or difficult to follow

concepts.name: user_intent
concepts.gloss: the user's intent U that the assistant should attempt to understand and follow in situation S
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of the user's intent in these cases, so a relation between the situation and the intent must exist

concepts.name: followable_intent
concepts.gloss: intent U is clear enough that the assistant can understand and follow it
concepts.inference: the clause distinguishes cases where intent is unclear from cases where it can be followed; this class marks the latter

concepts.name: no_instructions
concepts.gloss: a situation in which there are no instructions at all
concepts.inference: the clause describes cases with no instructions; this class marks such situations

concepts.name: unclear_user_intent
concepts.gloss: the user's intent in situation S is unclear
concepts.inference: the clause distinguishes unclear intent from intent that can be followed; this class marks the former

concepts.name: agentic_context
concepts.gloss: a context in which the assistant acts on behalf of the user with real-world consequences, so user goals or values matter
concepts.inference: the clause refers to agentic contexts; this class marks such contexts

concepts.name: irreversible_cost_risk
concepts.gloss: acting on a misunderstanding in situation S could cause irreversible costs
concepts.inference: the clause says to minimize expected irreversible costs that could arise from a misunderstanding; this class marks situations where such costs are possible

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: the assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document

asserts.read_back: responding to an ambiguous instruction % by attempting to understand and follow the user's intent is expected
responding to a situation % with no instructions by attempting to understand and follow the user's intent is expected
responding to an ambiguous instruction % with an unclear user intent by providing a robust answer or a safe guess, stating assumptions and asking clarifying questions as appropriate, is expected

responding to a situation % with no instructions and an unclear user intent by providing a robust answer or a safe guess, stating assumptions and asking clarifying questions as appropriate, is expected
in an agentic context with unclear user intent, erring on the side of caution to minimize expected irreversible costs from a misunderstanding is expected
in an agentic context with no instructions and unclear user intent, erring on the side of caution to minimize expected irreversible costs from a misunderstanding is expected

closure.reason: the clause obliges attempting to follow intent for ambiguous instructions but does not forbid other responses; silence permits
the clause obliges attempting to follow intent when no instructions exist but does not forbid other responses; silence permits
the clause obliges robust answers or safe guesses with assumptions and clarifying questions but does not forbid other responses; silence permits
the clause describes a preferred response when intent is unclear; it does not forbid other responses
the clause describes a preferred response when intent is unclear; it does not forbid other responses
the clause says to state assumptions as appropriate; it does not forbid omitting them in inappropriate cases
the clause says to ask clarifying questions as appropriate; it does not forbid omitting them in inappropriate cases
the clause obliges caution in agentic contexts with unclear goals but does not forbid other responses; silence permits
